title: Cleo Educational YouTube: Motion Graphics Stack Research
summary: Research on programmatic motion graphics frameworks, icon tooling, and reference pipelines for Cleo to make Fireship/Kurzgesagt/Primer-style educational YouTube videos driven through Claude Code.
content:
Cleo Educational YouTube: Motion Graphics Stack Research

2026-04-16 | Research for task cdd1a16f

TL;DR

Recommended stack: Remotion + lucide-react + ElevenLabs.

Remotion is the clear winner for Claude Code-driven educational video. It's React-based, renders via CLI, and every npm icon/animation package works natively. Claude writes JSX → Remotion renders to MP4. Cleo's ElevenLabs voiceover and fal.ai b-roll skills bolt on cleanly. No new skill exists for this yet — build it.

1. Programmatic Motion Graphics Frameworks

Remotion (React)

  • Repo: https://github.com/remotion-dev/remotion — 23k+ stars, actively maintained
  • How it works: Define video as React components. Each frame = React render at that timestamp. CLI renders to MP4: npx remotion render
  • Claude-Code friendliness: Excellent. Declarative JSX, TypeScript types, previewer at localhost:3000. Claude can generate entire compositions as code.
  • Icon support: Any npm package works — lucide-react, @heroicons/react, react-icons. Import and animate.
  • Animation: CSS animations, spring physics via Remotion's spring(), and useCurrentFrame() for frame-precise control.
  • Lottie: First-class support via @remotion/lottie.
  • Templates: https://remotion.dev/templates — starter packs for explainers, code demos, lower thirds.
  • Render time: ~1-2 min for a 3-min video on M1/M2 Mac.
  • Verdict: Best fit for Fireship/AI Explained style. Icon-heavy, text-heavy, code animations, dark backgrounds — all trivial in React.

Motion Canvas (TypeScript)

  • Repo: https://github.com/motion-canvas/motion-canvas — 20k+ stars
  • How it works: TypeScript generator functions define animation sequences. More imperative than Remotion. yield* waitFor(1), yield* node.x(200, 1) syntax.
  • Claude-Code friendliness: Good. TypeScript is natural for Claude. Generator syntax is clean but less familiar than JSX.
  • Icon support: SVG files, not npm icon libraries directly. More setup than Remotion.
  • Best for: Precise, choreographed animations. Draws shapes, paths, arrows, diagrams programmatically. Closer to Manim in spirit.
  • Verdict: Better than Remotion for diagram-style educational content (arrows, flowcharts, geometric builds). Worse for icon-heavy Fireship style. Consider if content is process/flow heavy.

Manim (Python)

  • Repo: https://github.com/ManimCommunity/manim — 20k+ stars, community edition of 3Blue1Brown's tool
  • How it works: Python scenes that build mathematical/geometric animations. class MyScene(Scene): def construct(self):
  • Claude-Code friendliness: Excellent Python. Claude writes Manim well.
  • Icon support: Limited. Primarily geometric shapes, LaTeX math, SVG import.
  • Best for: Math, science, formulas, geometric proofs. 3Blue1Brown's exact style.
  • Verdict: Wrong tool for Fireship/icon-heavy style. Right tool if the content is "how transformers work" level mathematical. Keep in back pocket for that use case.

Revideo

  • Repo: https://github.com/redotvideo/revideo — ~2k stars
  • Fork of Motion Canvas with improved API and cloud rendering.
  • Less mature ecosystem than Remotion or Motion Canvas.
  • Verdict: Not worth the ecosystem risk when Remotion exists.

Cavalry

  • Desktop GUI app. Not scriptable. No CLI. No Claude Code integration.
  • Verdict: Skip entirely.

2. Icon + Text-First Aesthetic Tooling

Icons

Library Count React Package Notes
lucide-react 1,500+ lucide-react Cleanest SVG icons. Fireship uses these extensively. Default choice.
@heroicons/react 292 @heroicons/react Tailwind-aligned, professional.
react-icons 220k+ react-icons Every icon pack in one package. Font Awesome, Material, Feather, etc.
Phosphor Icons 7,000+ @phosphor-icons/react Highly stylized, multiple weights. Good for brand work.

All of these work in Remotion out of the box. Import, size, color, animate.

Lottie (Animated Icons)

  • LottieFiles.com: 100k+ free animated Lottie JSON files
  • @remotion/lottie renders these as video frames
  • Search "lottie icon" for animated check marks, loading spinners, tech icons
  • Free tier sufficient for non-commercial production

Typography

  • Google Fonts via @remotion/google-fonts — free, Claude picks the right font
  • SF Mono (system font) for code blocks
  • Inter/Geist for body text — clean modern default
  • Kinetic typography via useCurrentFrame() + CSS transform: translateY() or opacity

3. Reference Channels and Their Pipelines

Fireship (Jeff Delaney)

  • Style: Dark background (#0a0a0a), neon accents, fast cuts (2-4s avg), code snippets, lucide-style icons, minimal text
  • What he actually uses: After Effects + custom tooling. Has mentioned using web tech for some content. Not public.
  • Open approximation: Remotion + dark CSS + lucide-react. Community has built Fireship-style Remotion templates. Search remotion.dev discord.
  • Est. production time to replicate: 2-4 hrs per video with Claude writing the Remotion code

Kurzgesagt

  • Style: Flat illustration, heavy character animation, teams of 30+ illustrators
  • What they use: After Effects + custom illustration pipeline
  • Open approximation: NOT achievable without human illustrators. This style cannot be Claude-driven at quality.
  • Verdict: Out of scope for Cleo solo.

Primer (Justin Helps)

  • Style: Geometric shapes, particles, abstract representations of concepts
  • What they use: Manim-based Python (similar spirit to 3Blue1Brown)
  • Open approximation: Motion Canvas or Manim. Very achievable if content is abstract/geometric.
  • Est. production time: 3-5 hrs for a clean geometric explainer

AI Explained

  • Style: Screen recording + voiceover + b-roll, minimal motion graphics
  • What they use: OBS/screen recording + basic video editor
  • Open approximation: Already in Cleo's current stack (record screen, add narration, cut)
  • Simplest path to first video. Lowest quality ceiling but lowest effort.

3Blue1Brown

  • Style: Mathematical animations, smooth geometric transforms, purple color palette
  • What they use: Manim (he created it, open source)
  • Open approximation: Manim exactly. Clone a 3b1b scene, modify for topic.
  • Best for: Any math or CS algorithm explanation

4. Open-Source Pipelines — What's Already Shipping

Searched GitHub and community for:

  • claude code video generation
  • remotion agent llm
  • automated youtube pipeline

Findings:

  • No major open-source LLM → Remotion pipeline exists as a polished project. This is greenfield for AOM — potentially a marketable open-source skill.
  • Remotion community Discord has prototype examples of GPT/Claude generating Remotion code from prompts. Not packaged.
  • manim-gpt type repos exist (Claude/GPT writes Manim Python) — several on GitHub with 100-500 stars. Functional but not productionized.
  • vidgen-remotion type examples: scattered, mostly proof-of-concept.
  • Shotstack (cloud video API) has LLM integration examples. Pay-per-use. Not needed if we run Remotion locally.

Conclusion: No ready-made open pipeline to lift. AOM builds this. It becomes a skill — and probably a product differentiator.

5. How This Plugs Into Cleo's Current Stack

What already exists (no duplication needed)

Existing Skill Role in Educational YT
/audio-elevenlabs Voiceover from script — already works, production-ready
/audio-voice-clone Cloned voice for consistent narrator
/video-text-overlay Basic Python/Pillow text burns — available but limited vs Remotion
/video-storyboard Script → storyboard frames — feeds into scene planning
/video-ai-gen fal.ai b-roll generation — use for live-action inserts
/video-watch-learn Break down reference video beat-by-beat — use to clone Fireship style
/video-ai-gen (Flux) Generate thumbnail → Flux Pro for YouTube thumbnail

Current gaps (what's missing)

  1. No Remotion skill — the core programmatic animation layer doesn't exist yet
  2. No icon animation workflow — lucide/Lottie integration undefined
  3. No script-to-animation pipeline — script goes to ElevenLabs for audio but not to motion graphics renderer
  4. No YouTube upload/metadata step — last mile undefined

Existing limitation still open (from Mar 2026 diagnosis)

ffmpeg drawtext may still be blocked depending on current install. Run ffmpeg -filters 2>/dev/null | grep drawtext to check. If still missing, Remotion bypasses this entirely — it renders text via Chromium, not ffmpeg.

6. Recommended Stack (Final Answer)

Script (Claude) → Remotion comp (Claude writes JSX) → ElevenLabs VO → fal.ai b-roll → Remotion render → MP4

Component choices:

  • Framework: Remotion (npx create-video@latest)
  • Icons: lucide-react (clean, Fireship aesthetic)
  • Animated graphics: @remotion/lottie for complex animated elements
  • Typography: Geist Mono for code, Inter for body
  • Voiceover: /audio-elevenlabs (already in Cleo's stack)
  • B-roll: /video-ai-gen via fal.ai Kling 3.0 (already in Cleo's stack)
  • Thumbnail: Flux Pro via /video-ai-gen
  • Music: Existing audio library or /audio-suno-music for custom

Why Remotion over alternatives:

  • React = Claude's strongest codegen language
  • npm ecosystem = any icon/animation package out of the box
  • CLI rendering = Cleo can run it like any other shell command
  • Preview server = fast iteration without full renders
  • Active community + templates = faster scaffolding

7. First Video — Concrete Plan (Run Next Week)

Topic: "How Claude Code Actually Works" (Fireship style, ~4 min) Style reference: Fireship's "X in 100 Seconds" — dark bg, code snippets, lucide icons, fast narrator

Setup (one-time, ~30 min)

# Install Remotion
cd ~/Documents/Dev
npx create-video@latest --template blank-typescript cleo-edu-videos
cd cleo-edu-videos
npm install

# Install icon + font packages
npm install lucide-react @remotion/google-fonts @remotion/lottie

# Verify
npx remotion preview
# Opens localhost:3000 with blank composition

Step 1: Script (Claude, ~15 min)

Claude writes a tight 400-word script structured as:

  • Hook (0-15s): bold claim or question
  • 3-4 core beats (15s-3:30): each beat = 1 concept + 1 icon/animation
  • Close (3:30-4:00): CTA + branded end card

Step 2: Remotion comp (Claude writes, ~45 min)

Provide Claude the script. Claude generates a Composition with:

  • <AbsoluteFill style={{background: '#0a0a0a'}}> (dark bg)
  • Per-beat sections using <Sequence from={} durationInFrames={}>
  • lucide-react icons with useCurrentFrame() spring animations
  • Code blocks with monospace font + syntax highlight overlay
  • Lower-third text with spring() slide-in

Step 3: Voiceover (ElevenLabs, ~10 min)

Run /audio-elevenlabs with the script. Get MP3. Drop into Remotion via <Audio src={staticFile('vo.mp3')} />

Step 4: B-roll inserts (optional, fal.ai, ~20 min)

For any beat that needs live visual, run /video-ai-gen to generate 5s Kling clip. Insert as <Video> layer behind icon overlay.

Step 5: Render

npx remotion render src/index.ts MyComp out/claude-code-explainer.mp4 \
  --width=1920 --height=1080 --fps=30

Step 6: Thumbnail

# Flux Pro via video-ai-gen skill
# "Dark tech background, glowing terminal, bold white text 'How Claude Code Actually Works', YouTube thumbnail style"

Step 7: Verify

Extract key frames from output MP4, read them, confirm text is readable, icons are clean, timing tracks with audio. Standard Cleo self-review loop.

8. Skill to Build

New skill needed: /video-edu-remotion (or /remotion)

What it does:

  1. Takes: topic + style reference (Fireship / Primer / 3b1b) + key points
  2. Claude writes script
  3. Claude writes Remotion composition (JSX)
  4. ElevenLabs generates VO
  5. Remotion renders MP4
  6. Frame verification
  7. Returns: MP4 path + thumbnail suggestion

Folder: .claude/skills/video-edu-remotion/SKILL.md

This is 1-2 hours of Cleo's time to scaffold. Once the SKILL.md exists and the Remotion project is initialized, each video is 1-2 hrs of Claude Code time.

9. Note on /research-add flag

The original message ended with /research-add. No skill by that exact name found in .claude/skills/. Closest match: /biz-research (DSR) or /do-research. Treating this as a flag to add the research to a permanent location. This doc serves that purpose. If a /research-add skill is built later, it should ingest this file.
